title: Decentralized Object Store & Sync Engine — architecture as built

elements.name: Object API client
elements.description: S3-style API consumer. Puts, gets, heads, deletes and lists objects through any node.

elements.name: Operator
elements.description: Runs objnode processes, starts bucket migrations, reads membership and health.

elements.name: Developer or reader
elements.description: Runs simulation scenarios and replays a failing seed with the printed command.

elements.name: Decentralized Object Store & Sync Engine
elements.description: Leaderless, multi-region object store with node-level metadata sync. A cluster of objnode peers; every node accepts reads and writes.

elements.name: Peer objnode nodes
elements.description: Other instances of the same system, in the same region and in other regions, as seen from one node.

elements.name: DST harness
elements.description: Deterministic simulation harness (internal/sim, internal/sim/simtest, cmd/objsim). Test system: a single-threaded discrete-event loop with virtual clock, seeded PRNG streams, fault-injecting network and disk, and nemesis.

elements.name: cmd/objnode
elements.description: The node binary: reads flags or a JSON config file, builds the node runtime and the HTTP server, and stops both on a signal or when the node loop fails.

elements.name: Node runtime (internal/noderuntime)
elements.description: The real environment and the node loop: UDP datagrams and TCP request/response frames, the file disk, the wall clock with loop-posted timers, and the one goroutine that owns all protocol state. Runtime implements the object API's Service interface by posting every call to that loop.
elements.technology: Go; UDP, TCP length-prefixed frames, files

elements.name: Node core (internal/node)
elements.description: The one single-threaded Node that both the simulator and the real runtime execute. It builds gossip, storage, OCC metadata, the metadata Merkle worker and the saga engine over one environment, each on its own channel of the one transport, and implements the interfaces they declare: Membership for storage, Merkle and OCC, Repairer over the metadata keys, and MigrationOps. It holds the object and bucket operations, the shard inventory with repair and collection, and the loss declaration.

elements.name: Object API (internal/storage/httpapi)
elements.description: HTTP object API: the handler, the one status table, the request limits and the server. It declares the Service interface it calls. Bucket create, object put, get, head, delete and list, tags, ACL, quota, object metadata, migration start and status, members and health. Writes are conditional on If-Match or If-None-Match: *, and object responses carry an ETag. The request and response types and the API error sentinels are in internal/storage (api.go).

elements.name: Storage engine (internal/storage)
elements.description: Shard format, local chunk store, striping, manifest, shard placement, and the node that runs the put and get paths and serves shard requests.

elements.name: Erasure coding (internal/erasure)
elements.description: GF(2^8) arithmetic and the Reed-Solomon encoder and decoder.

elements.name: Gossip membership (internal/gossip)
elements.description: SWIM membership as one single-threaded node: probe, indirect probe through relays, suspicion with refutation by incarnation, piggybacked dissemination with a retransmit limit, periodic push-pull sync, join and leave, and the Membership view with change events. Expired dead and left entries become bounded tombstones. It uses Clock, Rand and Transport and no Disk.
plannedNotes: As built, the one reader of the Membership view is the node core (internal/node), which answers the Membership interfaces of storage, Merkle and OCC from it.

elements.name: Merkle anti-entropy (internal/merkle)
elements.description: Fixed-depth 16-ary SHA-256 hash tree over a key-to-hash map with O(1) snapshots; a diff protocol that walks one tree level per round trip, with every reply at most 1 MiB; a wire codec; and an anti-entropy worker that scrubs local data by re-hashing it, diffs against one peer per period and pulls the keys that differ through the Repairer interface. It uses Clock, Rand and Transport and no Disk: stored bytes are reached only through the Repairer.
plannedNotes: As built, the node core (internal/node) implements Repairer over the OCC metadata keys and Membership from the gossip view; one worker per node covers all metadata. Shards are repaired by the node core with two local trees per bucket, not through the worker.
The package has no tombstones. The node core keeps a deleted key in the tree as its OCC tombstone version, which wins the merge against a stale live version.

elements.name: OCC metadata (internal/occ)
elements.description: Optimistic concurrency control for metadata. Each key holds exactly one version on every replica. Conditional writes (If-Match on an ETag, If-None-Match) refuse stale writers. When two concurrent versions meet, last-writer-wins picks one as a function of the pair alone: the higher hybrid logical clock stamp, then the node ID, then the version ID. The other is discarded, and every such discard is counted, logged and reported through a callback. Version vectors only classify a replacement as a causal overwrite or a concurrent discard. Quota check-and-set with a recount hook, a typed metadata document, and a replicating node that exchanges digests and documents with peers from its own Membership interface. It uses Clock, Rand, Transport and Disk; the Disk holds one state blob.
plannedNotes: As built, the one caller is the node core (internal/node), which also supplies the Membership interface from the gossip view.

Replaces the CRDT metadata layer of the first design by owner ruling (OCC amendment, 2026-11-21). Keeping concurrent versions as siblings was ruled out in favour of last-writer-wins with every discard recorded.
The package reports quota-key discards through OnDiscard and offers RecountQuota; it does not schedule recounts. The node core decides when a recount runs.
Tombstones are kept forever, and a mismatched replication round exchanges whole documents.

elements.name: Saga engine (internal/saga)
elements.description: Durable saga engine: orchestrator, checksummed log, recovery and retry policy; the five-step bucket-migration workflow, written against the MigrationOps interface; a model cluster (internal/saga/sagasim) that stands in for the real stores in tests.
plannedNotes: As built, MigrationOps has two implementations: the model cluster's, and migrator in internal/node on the real storage, Merkle and metadata packages.

elements.name: Environment interfaces (internal/env)
elements.description: The four interfaces protocol code sees: Clock, Rand, Transport, Disk; shared sentinels.

elements.name: Node disk
elements.description: Named blobs under the node's data directory: shard files, the OCC state blob and the saga logs.
elements.technology: Files: temp file, fsync, rename; directory fsync on Sync

elements.name: Join and leave
elements.description: Node.Join and Node.Leave (node.go). Join sends the push-pull sync to every seed at once and completes on the first reply, or fails with ErrJoinFailed and each seed's cause; its callback never runs inside Join. Seeds from Config.Seeds and from Join are remembered, at most MaxSeeds (256). While the node knows no live member but itself it re-joins its seeds every probe period. Leave marks the node left, tells every live member in one gossip datagram, stops the timers and closes the node.

elements.name: Probe
elements.description: onTick and nextTarget (node.go). One ping per ProbeInterval to the next live member in shuffled round-robin order; a member that becomes live in mid-round is inserted at a random later position. A target with no ack, direct or relayed, by the next tick becomes suspect.

elements.name: Indirect probe
elements.description: onProbeTimeout, onPingReq and the relay table (node.go). After ProbeTimeout without an ack, asks k random other live members (IndirectProbes, default 3) to ping the target. A relay pings with its own sequence number and forwards the ack with the requester's; a relay entry lasts one probe interval, at most MaxRelays (1,024) are held, and none is kept for a ping that could not be sent.

elements.name: Suspicion state machine
elements.description: suspectLocally, startSuspicion and refute (node.go). A member that becomes suspect, by a failed probe or by gossip, gets a timer of SuspicionMult x ceil(log2 N) x ProbeInterval; if it is still suspect at that incarnation when the timer fires it is declared dead. A node refutes any claim about itself, other than alive at its own incarnation, by raising its incarnation; it cannot go past the maximum uint32.

elements.name: Piggybacked dissemination
elements.description: enqueue, piggyback and sendWith (node.go). One queue entry per member. Every datagram the node sends carries updates within MaxPacket: explicit leads, then the destination's own entry if it is not alive, then the queue, fewest transmissions first. An entry is dropped after RetransmitMult x ceil(log2 N) transmissions. Updates on an inbound datagram are handed to the view's merge.

elements.name: Full-state sync
elements.description: syncWith, onSync and OnRequest (node.go). Push-pull: the caller sends its whole view, the receiver merges it and replies with its merged view, the caller merges that. Every SyncInterval a node syncs with one random live member and one random heal target taken from the dead entries in its view, its dead tombstones and its remembered seeds that are not live.

elements.name: Membership view and change events
elements.description: View, the pure merge lattice ordered by (incarnation, state, region) through Supersedes (member.go), and the node's merge step, Node.apply (node.go). Exposes the Membership interface (Members, Lookup, Subscribe) and five event kinds, delivered synchronously: joined, suspected, recovered, died, left. Holds at most MaxMembers entries. A dead or left entry stays for DeadRetention, then becomes a tombstone; at most MaxTombstones (4,096) are kept and the oldest is evicted.
plannedNotes: Retention followed by bounded tombstones was added by the build; PLAN.md names only the view and its events.

elements.name: Wire codec
elements.description: Message, Encode and Decode (wire.go) and the wire error codes 80 to 84 (errors.go). Version 1, big-endian. Ping, ack, ping-req and gossip are datagram kinds; sync request and sync response travel only as requests. Decoding is strict and canonical: every accepted byte string re-encodes to itself. This code does no I/O.
plannedNotes: Added by the build; PLAN.md does not name it.

elements.name: GF(2^8) arithmetic
elements.description: Field GF(2^8), polynomial 0x11D, generator 2; exp/log tables and a full 256-by-256 multiplication table; MulAddSlice for whole shards.

elements.name: Matrix inversion
elements.description: Gauss-Jordan matrix inversion over GF(2^8) (Matrix.Invert); a singular matrix is ErrSingular.

elements.name: Systematic Cauchy coding matrix
elements.description: Coding matrix [I | C] with C a Cauchy matrix; k + m at most 256.

elements.name: Encode
elements.description: Codec.Encode: computes the m parity shards from the k data shards. Split cuts a stripe into the k data shards first.

elements.name: Reconstruct
elements.description: Codec.Reconstruct and ReconstructData: rebuild missing shards from the first k present ones; more than m losses returns ErrTooFewShards. Join puts the data shards back together.

elements.name: Verify
elements.description: Codec.Verify: recomputes the parity and reports the first mismatch (ErrParityMismatch). It finds an inconsistent stripe; it does not locate the bad shard.
plannedNotes: No product code calls Verify. The storage engine finds damaged shards by checksum and passes them to Reconstruct as missing.

elements.name: Tree builder
elements.description: Tree in tree.go: New, Build, Set, Delete, Get, Root, Snapshot, DepthFor. A trie of fixed depth 1 to 16 and fanout 16 on the first 64 bits of SHA-256(key); leaves hold their entries sorted by key. Leaf and inner hashes are domain-separated by a tag byte, and an inner hash also covers its level; an empty subtree is the all-zero hash. Nodes are immutable: Set and Delete copy one path, and Snapshot is O(1). Limits: keys of at most 1,024 bytes, at most 4,096 entries per leaf.
plannedNotes: Kept in memory only and rebuilt from the stored data at every start.

elements.name: Diff protocol
elements.description: diff.go. Session is the asking side: a state machine over a snapshot of the local tree that produces one request per tree level and takes the reply through Feed. Tree.Answer is the answering side and holds no state between requests. Leaf entries are packed into replies of at most 1 MiB; a leaf that does not fit is cut and resumed. At most Limits.Frontier mismatched nodes (default 1,024, at most 2,040) go on to the next level; the rest are dropped and the result is marked Truncated. Every reply is validated, so a session ends within Depth + 5 x Frontier round trips whatever the peer sends. Compare runs a whole diff in memory. This code does no I/O.

elements.name: Anti-entropy worker
elements.description: Worker in worker.go: NewWorker, Start, Stop, Record, Forget, OnRequest, Stats. Each jittered period it re-reads and re-hashes the next batch of stored keys, so that rotted, missing and unreadable data shows in its tree (the scrub), then starts a round if none is in flight: picks one peer at random from Membership, diffs, and pulls each key whose remote hash the Repairer accepts. Pull-only: a node repairs itself. A round has a deadline; a failed round is abandoned whole and the next period is the retry. Stop ends the round in flight with ErrClosed.
plannedNotes: No tombstones: Forget removes a key from the tree, and a later round with a peer that still has the key would pull it back.

elements.name: Repairer interface
elements.description: Repairer in worker.go, declared by the package: Keys, Read, Valid, Fetch, Put. The worker's only way to stored bytes, local or on a peer. Valid decides which hash is right for a key; fetched bytes are stored only when their SHA-256 passes it.
plannedNotes: The node core implements it over the OCC metadata keys (metaRepairer); the package's tests implement it over a test chunk store.

elements.name: Wire codec
elements.description: wire.go and errors.go. Encodes and decodes the diff request and the four reply kinds: inner, leaf, cut leaf and equal. Big-endian, minimal varints; decoding is strict and canonical: every accepted message re-encodes to the same bytes. Sets MaxReplyBytes (1 MiB) and MaxRequestNodes (2,040). Wire error codes 112 and 113 in the package's block 112 to 127. This code does no I/O.
plannedNotes: Added by the build; PLAN.md does not name it.

elements.name: Membership interface
elements.description: Membership in worker.go, declared by the package: Peers returns the candidate peer IDs. The worker sorts them, removes duplicates and its own ID, and picks one at random each round.
plannedNotes: Added by the build; PLAN.md does not name it.
The node core implements it from the gossip view.

elements.name: Replicating node
elements.description: Node (an env.Process), Client and the wire messages (node.go, wire.go, errors.go). Loads the state blob at start. Each jittered period it sends its document digest to one random peer; the peer answers match or its whole document; the node merges it and pushes its own document back if the two still differ. After each local write it sends the changed key as a datagram to two random peers. Serves remote get, put and delete. All writes go through Node methods, which persist and then broadcast; Reader() is read-only. Wire error codes 128 to 136 in the block 128 to 143, with 131 unassigned. Added in Chunk 6: Node.Merge, which folds a fetched document into the store with the same merge, discard record and persistence, for the metadata anti-entropy of internal/node.

elements.name: Membership interface
elements.description: Membership (node.go), declared by the package: Peers returns the candidate peer IDs; the node sorts them and removes duplicates and its own ID. StaticMembership is a fixed list.
plannedNotes: The node core supplies it from the gossip view.

elements.name: Typed metadata document
elements.description: meta.go. Seven key kinds over the same store: tags, ACL entries, quotas, object metadata, object manifests, a bucket's routing pointer and content type. Key builders and ParseKey, typed writes and typed reads. RecountObjects sums a bucket's live object sizes for a quota recount and returns an overflow error instead of wrapping.

elements.name: Quota check-and-set and recount
elements.description: quota.go. UpdateQuota reads the usage with the precondition to write it back under, computes, and writes conditionally, retrying only on a failed precondition and at most a given number of times. An unconditional quota write is refused. RecountQuota takes a recount hook and writes only when the stored usage differs.
plannedNotes: The package does not schedule recounts. Updates on two sides of a partition settle by last-writer-wins, and the quota-key discard is the signal for a recount.

elements.name: Store
elements.description: Store and Reader (store.go). Put, Delete and SetScalar check the precondition against the held version and install its causal successor with a stamp above the one it replaces. Merge takes in a peer's document. Every mutation is a transaction: apply, encode the state blob, call the Persist hook, and restore everything if the persist fails. Dots come from one counter per actor; the actor epoch is drawn at random without readable state and retired for a fresh one when a discard leaves a gap in the node's own dots. The state blob is checksummed; an unreadable one is treated as no state.

elements.name: Discard record
elements.description: In store.go. When a merge drops a version that the winner's writer had not seen, either a held version replaced or an incoming version rejected, the store records it: a persisted counter, a 64-entry readable tail, a persisted outbox, and, after the persist succeeds, one log line and the OnDiscard callback. A window of the last 256 (key, loser) pairs stops a re-sent loser from being recorded twice. The outbox is emitted again when a node opens its state, so a crash before the emission loses no record.
plannedNotes: Records are local to the node and are not replicated. One lost version can be recorded on several nodes; every record names the losing version ID.

elements.name: Document, last-writer-wins merge
elements.description: Doc (doc.go): a map from key to one Version. A merge keeps, per key, the greater version under the last-writer-wins order; it is commutative, associative, idempotent and has no error path. The digest is the SHA-256 of the canonical encoding. There is one version per key in memory, in the encoding and in the API.

elements.name: Version and record
elements.description: version.go and record.go. A Version has a dot, a causal context, a tombstone flag, a value, a stamp and a version ID (a SHA-256). Version.Compare is the last-writer-wins order: stamp, then version ID. Supersedes asks whether one version's writer had seen the other. A Record is the one optional version of a key. The ETag is the version ID. Preconditions: IfMatch, IfNoneMatch, Unconditional.

elements.name: Version vectors and dots
elements.description: vv.go, and Dot in version.go. An actor is a node ID and an epoch; a version vector maps actors to counters, with Compare, Descends and Join. Used for classification only: they tell whether the winner's writer had seen the loser, and never choose the winner.

elements.name: Hybrid logical clock
elements.description: hlc.go. Stamp (wall, logical counter, node ID) with a total order. HLC over env.Clock: Now returns a stamp above every earlier one; Observe takes in a remote stamp and refuses one more than an hour ahead of the local clock.

elements.name: Canonical encoding
elements.description: encoding.go, with Doc.Encode and Decode. Replicas holding the same versions produce the same bytes. Decoding is strict and bounded: a repeated or out-of-order key, a non-minimal varint, an oversized count and trailing bytes are rejected, and the result must re-encode to the input.

elements.name: Orchestrator
elements.description: saga.Engine (engine.go) and Policy (policy.go). Single-threaded. Every record is appended and synced before the engine acts on it. Steps before the pivot retry up to MaxAttempts with clock-driven backoff and jitter, then compensate in reverse order; the pivot aborts only on ErrPermanent; later steps and compensations retry until they succeed. Each call carries the idempotency key (saga ID, step).

elements.name: Saga log
elements.description: Record format of the per-saga log blob (log.go): append-only frames with a magic byte, a length and two CRC-32C checksums. AppendRecord encodes; DecodeLog returns the valid prefix, reads a strict prefix of a frame as a torn tail and anything else wrong as ErrLogCorrupt. This code does no I/O: the orchestrator and recovery make the env.Disk calls.

elements.name: Recovery
elements.description: Engine.Recover (engine.go) and the pure Resume state machine (resume.go). Reads each log, truncates a torn tail before anything is appended, validates every transition and plans the next action: run a step, abort, compensate or end. A corrupt log is left as found and reported.

elements.name: Bucket-migration workflow
elements.description: saga.Migration (migration.go): allocate, copy, verify, flip (the pivot), delete-source. delete-source reads the merged pointer, seals the source, runs a catch-up copy and a second root comparison, retires the source and then promotes the target; a migration that lost to another one cleans up its own target instead.

elements.name: Step interfaces
elements.description: MigrationOps (migration.go): the five small callback-style interfaces Allocator, Copier, Verifier, Router and Retirer that the workflow is written against.
plannedNotes: Two implementations: the model cluster's Ops, and migrator in internal/node.

elements.name: Model cluster (internal/saga/sagasim)
elements.description: Test-support package. Model stores, a coordinator process that hosts the Engine, and a writing client, all as simulator nodes; sagasim.Ops implements MigrationOps over env.Transport. It also exports the 78-cell failure-point matrix runner (Harness, Cells, Run) and the nemesis and duel scenario drivers, so the same runs can be repeated on real components.
plannedNotes: Added by the build; PLAN.md does not name it. The node core's tests and the end-to-end suite (test/e2e) reuse its failure-matrix runner on real nodes.

elements.name: Shard file format
elements.description: 64-byte header plus payload. The SHA-256 in the header covers the other header fields and the payload. Canonical blob names.

elements.name: Local chunk store
elements.description: Chunk store over env.Disk: write then sync, verified read, list, delete. A returned Put or Delete is durable.

elements.name: Object striping
elements.description: Fixed-size stripes (1 MiB of data by default) so multi-MB objects are coded stripe by stripe. Encodes a stripe into shard blobs; verifies shard blobs and decodes a stripe.

elements.name: Object manifest
elements.description: Per object version: size, content SHA-256, layout (k, m, stripe size), and for each shard of each stripe the node chosen and the blob checksum. Canonical binary encoding.

elements.name: Placement
elements.description: Region-aware placement by rendezvous hashing over a Membership interface declared in this package. Place for a new stripe; Replace for repair.

elements.name: Object put and get paths (Node)
elements.description: storage.Node. PUT succeeds when every stripe has k+1 durable shard acknowledgements and returns the manifest; GET reads any k verified shards per stripe. The same node serves shard put, get and delete requests from its chunk store.
plannedNotes: Default k=4, m=2 and the k+1 write threshold are PLAN.md OQ-15.
The package stores no manifest and has no object delete: the node core keeps the manifest in OCC metadata, and a delete is an OCC tombstone there.

elements.name: Shard request protocol
elements.description: Request format between nodes: an op byte (put, get or delete shard), the shard's blob name, and for put the shard blob. Errors return as wire codes 96 to 100.
plannedNotes: Added by the build; PLAN.md does not name it.

elements.name: Environment interfaces (internal/env)
elements.description: The same package as element c-env, shown as a neighbour in the component views of other packages. The four interfaces protocol code sees: Clock, Rand, Transport, Disk; shared sentinels.

elements.name: Storage engine (internal/storage)
elements.description: The same package as element c-storage, shown as a neighbour in the component views of other packages. Shard format, local chunk store, striping, manifest, shard placement, and the node that runs the put and get paths and serves shard requests.

elements.name: Node core (internal/node)
elements.description: The same package as element c-node, shown as a neighbour in the component views of other packages. It builds the protocol packages into one node and implements the interfaces they declare.

elements.name: Erasure coding (internal/erasure)
elements.description: The same package as element c-erasure, shown as a neighbour in the component views of other packages. GF(2^8) arithmetic and the Reed-Solomon encoder and decoder.

Records every concurrent version the merge drops, replaced or rejected, in the same durable write as the merge; emits after the persist succeeds
Takes a stamp for each write; observes every stamp of a received or loaded document
Encodes and decodes the checksummed state blob
Holds one version per key; a merge keeps the greater version under the last-writer-wins order
Equal documents encode to equal bytes; the digest is their SHA-256
Carries a dot and a causal context; Supersedes compares them. Classification only
Carries a stamp; the last-writer-wins order compares stamps first
Reads the node's clock
Draws a fresh actor epoch. The store makes no Disk call: it persists through the hook the node supplies
Reads the usage and writes it back under If-Match or If-None-Match, through the store's or the node's Put
Typed keys and values, written through the store's or the node's Put and read through Reader
RecountObjects supplies the usage a recount writes

Makes every metadata write through Node methods: Put and Delete under a precondition, SetScalar for system records, Merge for versions fetched by metadata anti-entropy or carried by a migration's shard check; reads through Reader; receives each discard through OnDiscard
Typed keys and writes: ManifestKey, QuotaKey and RouteKey, PutTag, PutACL, SetRoute, and Route on Reader. The object record under the manifest key is written with Put, not PutManifest
UpdateQuota with AddUsage on a put or delete; RecountQuota with its own recount over the live manifests, after a discard and in the quota audit
Creates the engine, recovers at start, begins a migration and reads its status; OnEnd reports a finished saga
Runs the steps of a registered definition: bounded retry with backoff before the pivot, compensation in reverse order
Encodes each record; the record is appended and synced before the step or compensation acts
Decodes the valid prefix of each log; tells a torn tail from corruption
Hands over the recovered snapshot; the orchestrator resumes or compensates from it
Claim, copy, root, flip pointer (pivot), seal, retire, promote; unclaim and discard to compensate
Lists and reads logs, truncates a torn tail, deletes an empty log; retry timer for an unreadable log
Appends and syncs records; step timeout and backoff timers; jitter

Implements MigrationOps as migrator: claims and registrations as metadata keys, the copy through a storage node of its own, a shard check on the holders (a write quorum per stripe) before a copy is staged, before the target root and before retire, the roots with merkle.Build, the flip with SetRoute, pointer agreement with every live peer, seal, retire with a purge of named dead versions, promote
Registers Migration(migrator) as the engine's definition; decodes the MigrationInput of each call
Its tests implement Harness.Build over real nodes and run the 78-cell failure matrix with Run
Checks each record against the same state machine before writing it, and takes its next action from it
Implements MigrationOps over the model stores (sagasim.Ops)
Its coordinator process hosts the Engine; the matrix runner freezes it at a chosen record through Config.Hook
Registers the migration definition; the matrix runner wraps its steps to inject failures
Requests between coordinator, stores and client; each store's state blob; client and reload retry timers
Builds the cluster as simulated nodes; crashes, torn crashes, the nemesis and invariants
Put on the storage node of the bucket's placement scope, Get by manifest; hands inbound shard requests to OnRequest after its own checks
Cuts objects into stripes; encodes and decodes each stripe
Split, Encode, ReconstructData and Join per stripe
Chooses a node for each shard of a stripe
Reads the candidate members through the Membership interface; the node core's gossipView and regionView answer from the gossip view
Serves shard put, get and delete requests from the local store
Sends shards to peers and fetches shards from peers (Transport); zero-delay callbacks and retry backoff (Clock); version IDs (Rand)
Header plus payload; SHA-256 verified on every write and read
Write then sync, verified read, list, delete
PUT fills in and returns the manifest; GET takes each shard's node and checksum from it
Stores the encoded manifest inside its object record in OCC metadata and decodes it for every read; the storage package stores no manifest
Shard inventory and repair through Node.Store: lists and reads shards for the scrub and for a migration's shard check, writes a rebuilt shard, deletes collected and purged shards
Wraps each shard in a header on encode; checks header and checksum on decode
Encodes requests to peers; decodes requests it serves
Names the shard by its canonical blob name
Calls the object service: each route is a method of the Service interface, which the API package declares and Runtime implements
Builds the one Node over the real environment; delivers datagrams and requests to it; posts each service call to the node loop, where it runs as a Node method
Reads the members to place shards on, through the Membership interface it declares; the node core answers from the gossip view, for all regions or for one
Reads its replication peers through the Membership interface it declares; the node core answers from the gossip view
Reads its peers through Membership and reaches the stored metadata through Repairer; the node core implements both
Runs the migration steps through MigrationOps; the node core's migrator implements them on storage, Merkle roots and OCC metadata, with a shard check on the holders of every copy
Builds the runtime from its options, starts it, waits for a signal or a loop failure, and shuts it down
Starts the HTTP server over the runtime, with the node core's status rows; shuts it down before the runtime
Implements Clock, Rand, Transport and Disk for the real runtime
Sends and receives datagrams and request/response frames; one TCP connection per request
Reads and writes named blobs (file-backed Disk)
Runs the same Node as a simulated process (node.NewFactory) in the full-node simulation tests, the conformance test and the end-to-end suite
Creates one worker per node for metadata, starts and stops it, records each written key, and passes it the peers' diff requests
Implements it: gossipView.Peers, the live members other than the node itself
Rebuild: DecodeStripe from the other holders' shards against the manifest checksums, then EncodeStripe to get its own shard back
Encodes get-shard requests for a rebuild; decodes inbound requests to refuse shard deletes and writes of a shard it recorded absent
